## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Nandattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 15) is a verse biographical poem in the Therāpadāna section of the *Apadāna* collection [SuttaCentral]. The text is preserved in the Pali Canon and SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the work across five languages [SuttaCentral].

In terms of text reuse and parallels, SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels, but DharmaNexus identifies substantial intra-Pali reuse and several cross-language alignments [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali tradition, significant portions of the poem are shared with the commentaries, including eleven matching segments each with the first part (§7.2–8.1) and second part (§0.3–1.3) of Dhammapāla's *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, as well as seven segments matching the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic and stock verse sequences are also shared with multiple other apadānas, notably the *Sakacintaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 63), *Khomadāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 32), *Mandāravapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 363), *Supāricariyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 163), and *Nāgasamālattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 73) [DharmaNexus].

In cross-language machine alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with Sanskrit narratives, most prominently the *Kaṭhināvadāna* (four matches, similarity score up to 75) and the *Mahāsudarśanāvadāna*, as well as two matches with the Chinese *Jiexia jing* (解夏經, T 63) [DharmaNexus].
